ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 10/2010 of 28 April 2010 on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended by Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 of 27 April 2021 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May 2014 implementing Law 10/2010; the Spanish beneficial ownership register (Registro de Titularidades Reales) under the Ministry of Justice and the General Tax Law (Ley 58/2003).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and certified copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's passport, plus address verification and criminal-record certificate where applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority, police, or notary in the owner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the origin state is not a party to the 1961 Hague Convention, consular legalization at the Spanish consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing for any corporate shareholder or corporate ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent corporate authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Spanish incorporation representative, with authenticated identity documentation of every foreign signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary after verification of foreign notarial/apostilled identification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for underlying foreign signatures; the Spanish notarial act itself requires no apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based KYC under Law 10/2010 before incorporation. All shareholders, directors, UBOs and relevant payment-rail counterparties must be screened against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the UN Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, and Spanish SEPBLAC/CNMV warning lists. PEP status is determined for senior management, board members, and UBOs; enhanced due diligence applies to high-risk jurisdictions; confirmed sanctions hits require refusal to proceed and a suspicious transaction report to SEPBLAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), with electronic name-clearing applications processed through the CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in characters compatible with the Spanish/Latin alphabet and must be grammatically coherent in Spanish or in a co-official Spanish language. Names originally in non-Latin scripts must be translated or transliterated; any resulting ambiguity or misleading resemblance to an existing name may cause rejection.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The 90-day name certificate cannot be extended. If the Registro Mercantil Central rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reposición) before the same registry within one month. If unsuccessful, an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) may be lodged with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within one month. In parallel, the applicant should reserve an alternative acceptable denomination to avoid delay in incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the initial e-commerce pet supplies business, provided the virtual registered office is a genuine physical location in Spain able to receive official correspondence and service of process. The address must appear in the deed and in the Commercial Registry. A virtual office cannot create artificial corporate substance if management and control are actually exercised in Spain; the General Tax Law anti-abuse rule under Article 15 will apply.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; quantified at approximately 5–10% annual likelihood for a low-risk, non-licensed e-commerce SL, rising if official post at the registered address goes unanswered, or if VAT and intra-community trade filings indicate anomalies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for negative name certificate (certificado de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff for one name-search application.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the incorporation deed, statutory bylaws, and first director appointment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary in the province of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff (arancel notarial) for a limited company with capital within the standard statutory range.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the deed in the Mercantile Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial registry tariff for inscription of the incorporation deed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional tax identification number (NIF) and company set-up via CIRCE
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Free administrative electronic procedure jointly handled by AEAT, notary, and registry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of foreign UBO documents and sworn Spanish translation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Source-country competent authority, Spanish consulate, and Spanish sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedules and prevailing translator rates for one complete foreign-document bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, sanctions, and UBO register screening and AML compliance file set-up
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External KYC/AML compliance provider or Spanish law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk e-commerce corporate onboarding under Law 10/2010.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized power of attorney for the local incorporation representative
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff for a corporate power of attorney.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation due diligence legal opinion, corporate documentation drafting, and advisory on Spanish tax registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish corporate and tax law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee based on prevailing Spanish market rates for formation and pre-incorporation advice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), approved by Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, particularly Articles 1, 4, 5, 19-23, 32, 33, 35, 62, 210-242 and 247-251; Commercial Registry Regulations, approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, under the Ministry of Justice and the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución) filed for registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry, commonly prepared through the Unified Electronic Document (Documento Único Electrónico) using CIRCE.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. Until the company reaches EUR 3,000 of capital, statutory safeguards apply: at least 20 percent of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may have supplementary liability up to the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital. No mandatory escrow account exists. A bank certificate evidencing cash contributions may be used, although founders may generally assume joint responsibility for the reality of cash contributions in the deed where legally permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the shareholders’ subscriptions for the entire share capital of the Company are acknowledged as fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [FULL SPANISH ADDRESS] is adopted and recorded for all corporate and registry purposes; (3) [NAME] is appointed sole director, or, alternatively, [NAMES] are appointed as joint or several directors as specified in the articles, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; and (4) the appointed officer is authorised to complete all notarial, tax, registry, banking and electronic filing actions required to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a negative certificate of corporate name (certificación negativa de denominación social), listing permitted alternative names. Apply online or through an authorised representative. Use the exact approved name in the deed and preserve the certificate for the notary.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names in priority order
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name or correct the identified similarity or legal-form issue. If the certificate expires, obtain a renewal or a new certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Tax Identification and Complete Foreign Shareholder Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), including its online tax-registration services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a provisional Spanish tax identification number for the company using Form 036 or the CIRCE/DUE process. Non-resident shareholders, directors and authorised representatives must obtain Spanish foreigner tax numbers where required. Foreign corporate documents must be apostilled or legalised and accompanied by an official Spanish translation unless an applicable exemption exists.
required_dossiers: NIE or Spanish tax identification evidence for relevant non-residents
Apostilled or legalised corporate powers and extracts, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically or through the assigned Tax Agency office to any identification or beneficial-ownership query. Correct Form 036 and resubmit supporting identification documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected by the founders, with electronic coordination through CIRCE where used
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notary with the approved name certificate, articles, shareholder and director information, registered-office evidence, capital contribution evidence or legally permitted founder declaration, beneficial-owner information and powers of attorney. Execute the public deed in Spanish or through an official interpreter. The notary verifies identity, capacity, legality and representation.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports, identity cards or corporate extracts
Registered-office title, lease or consent evidence
Bank certificate for cash contributions or legally permitted contribution declaration
Powers of attorney, apostilled or legalised where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure any notarial objection by amending the articles, correcting identity or authority evidence, supplying missing translations, or producing additional proof of capital and address before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronically authorised or paper public deed, articles and required tax-registration documentation with the competent registry. Pay the applicable registry tariff and publication charges. The registry reviews legality, corporate name, capital, governance, registered office and director appointments before issuing the registration entry.
required_dossiers: Tax identification application or provisional tax number
Power of attorney for the filing representative, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registrar issues a defect notice, obtain the written qualification, correct the deed or supporting documents through the notary where required, and resubmit within the applicable validity period. A negative qualification may be appealed to the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Social Security and Beneficial-Ownership Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency, General Treasury of Social Security and the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, obtain or confirm the definitive tax identification number and file the census declaration. Register the company as an employer before hiring personnel, register directors or employees under the appropriate Social Security regime, and maintain current beneficial-ownership information through the applicable Commercial Registry systems.
required_dossiers: Employment and payroll information, if personnel will be hired
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic filings, provide missing registration evidence, and request rectification from the relevant authority. Do not commence employment activity until required Social Security registrations are effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Corporate Books and Governance Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry through its electronic book-legalisation platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legalise the mandatory corporate books electronically, including the shareholders' register and minutes book. Establish director signing authorities, conflict-of-interest controls, accounting records, annual accounts procedures and approval calendars. File annual accounts and required corporate documents within statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected book legalisation or annual-account filings and resubmit electronically. Rectify governance defects through properly convened shareholder or board resolutions and preserve the correction trail.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No sector-specific industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for electronic retailing of pet supplies. Where a warehouse or physical premises is used, the relevant Autonomous Community industrial authority and the municipality where the premises is located may impose activity, installation, opening, zoning or safety requirements.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No national manufacturing or sector-specific operating permit for ordinary online retail of pet supplies; municipal activity or opening declaration (declaración responsable de actividad or licencia de apertura), where required, applies to physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, together with the competent environmental authority of the relevant Autonomous Community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from environmental impact assessment for ordinary ecommerce and retail warehousing with no listed industrial project, subject to confirmation of the site's activity, scale and local environmental rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No special process-emission limits normally apply to ordinary retail operations. The company must prevent unlawful wastewater discharge, comply with municipal sewer conditions, manage packaging and commercial waste through authorised systems, and comply with applicable waste, chemicals, refrigerant, battery and electrical-equipment rules. Any VOC, hazardous-waste or industrial discharge activity may trigger separate permits and sector-specific limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a warehouse or retail premises, obtain the applicable municipal activity or opening clearance, fire-prevention compliance evidence and, where required, an installation certificate from a qualified technician. Maintain emergency plans, extinguishers, evacuation routes, electrical and structural safety documentation, and occupational-risk-prevention compliance. No general national civil-defence licence is required solely for online retail.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Spanish Tax Agency; electronic portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Registration forms: Modelo 036/037 (census registration) and Modelo 030 (non-resident NIF application).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Spanish SL: (1) incorporate before a notary and file the company deed at the Registro Mercantil; (2) obtain the provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal, formerly CIF) by submitting Modelo 036 to AEAT; (3) complete the definitive NIF upon registry inscription. Foreign non-resident entities transacting in Spain without a permanent establishment must request a non-resident NIF (T/W code) via Modelo 030 and appoint an AEAT fiscal representative. E-commerce operators may alternatively register for the EU One Stop Shop (OSS/IOSS) scheme from their Member State of establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain applies a general pure corporate tax regime (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Ley 27/2014) with no check-the-box entity classification. Available elections include: (i) tax consolidation for a Spanish group holding at least 70% of a subsidiary's capital (art. 62 et seq. LIS); (ii) OSS / Import-OSS optional registration for intra-EU and low-value import distance sales; (iii) special SME cash-basis VAT election (art. 163 undecies LIVA, optional up to EUR 2,000,000 turnover); (iv) depreciation method elections (linear vs. reducing balance) and the 15% reduced corporate rate for newly created entities in their first two profit-making years; (v) hybrid mismatch reporting and compliance under ATAD transposition (Ley 4/2023) with mandatory annual DAC6 disclosure rather than elective deferral.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and RD 1624/1992
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold exempts an established Spanish company from VAT registration – compulsory from the first taxable supply (Modelo 036). Simplified and turnover-based regimes apply only to small traders (annual turnover up to EUR 100,000; purchases up to EUR 250,000). For non-established EU sellers, the intra-EU distance sales threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year across all EU Member States. Non-EU sellers supplying imported goods valued at EUR 150 or less to consumers may use IOSS without local registration; otherwise a Spanish VAT number and a local fiscal representative are required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Anti-Fraud Ley 11/2021. Large businesses (turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000) and VAT groups must file near-real-time transactional records under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) within 4 business days. AEAT is progressively rolling out the fully real-time 'Verifactu' clearance framework (certified billing software, digital stamping, and immediate supply of invoicing events – TIVE) with implementing decrees pending through 2025-2026. Invoices must be machine-readable and contain mandatory fields; uncertified or tampered invoicing software is penalized up to EUR 50,000.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods to third countries are zero-rated under art. 21 LIVA when the goods physically leave the EU within 3 months of supply and proof of exit is retained. Intra-EU B2B supplies are exempt at 0% where the customer's valid VIES VAT number is recorded and the recapitulative statement (Modelo 349) is filed. B2B cross-border services for e-commerce (platform and marketplace services, logistics, advertising, software, payment processing) follow the reverse-charge place-of-supply rules under arts. 69-70 LIVA and are zero-rated when the recipient is established outside Spain; B2C digital services to non-EU consumers are outside Spanish VAT under the place-of-consumption rule. The EU import distance-sale exemption allows 0% on low-value parcel imports when IOSS is used.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document / Customs Export Declaration (DUA, SAD EX-A/EX-B) with AEAT clearance and MRN (Movement Reference Number)
Transport documentation evidencing EU exit: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note with exit validation
Commercial invoice and packing list mirroring the customs declaration
Evidence of consideration: inward remittance certificate / bank credit statement (Certificado de recepción de fondos del exterior) and collection or set-off proofs
For intra-EU supplies: VIES-registered customer VAT number and the recapitulative statement (Modelo 349) filing
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT customs and VAT audits may reopen the four prior tax years (art. 66 LGT). Failure to substantiate EU exit (incomplete DUA, missing transport proof, or void export documentation) triggers retrospective zero-rating clawback with late-payment interest under arts. 26 and 87 LIVA. Incorrect invoicing or omission of VAT constitutes an 'infracción grave' under art. 193 LGT, yielding fines of 50% to 100% of the amount involved (150% where fraud is present), plus the surcharge of 10% to 20% under art. 27 LGT. Export document falsification may be criminally prosecuted under art. 305 Código Penal when the defrauded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, with penalties of up to 5 years' imprisonment and fines of up to six times the defrauded amount. Anti-Fraud Ley 11/2021 additionally imposes autonomous penalties for billing-software tampering (up to EUR 50,000) and the loss of favorable exporter status with AEAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the central bank, monetary authority and foreign-exchange statistical regulator of the Kingdom of Spain; external capital-movement supervision is shared with the Dirección General de Política Comercial y de Inversiones Exteriores within the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Spain. Spain applies the EC Treaty freedom of capital movements (Article 63 TFEU), allowing complete convertibility for both current-account (trade in goods/services, remittances) and capital-account (direct investment, credits, financial loans, portfolio flows) operations. As an EU member and Eurozone participant, Spain maintains no exchange-control bottleneck or approval requirement for profit/dividend remittance to non-resident shareholders. Remitted dividends and branch profits are nevertheless subject to Spanish non-resident-income-tax withholding (generally 19% under Spain's internal law, reduced to 0-15% under an applicable double-tax treaty) and require prior filing of the non-resident income tax return and, where the beneficiary is in a tax-haven jurisdiction, heightened substance verification. Cuban, Venezuelan or Syrian payments would likewise be screened, but no general convertibility limitation exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation in Spain or the Eurozone, no mandated conversion of export income into euro, and no fixed repatriation timeline. Exporters may retain settlement in foreign currency, but are required to register each non-resident payment in the Bank of Spain's Exterior Transactions ('Operaciones con el Exterior') statistical system when aggregated monthly transfers in one currency and concept exceed the reporting threshold (typically EUR 1,000,000, or EUR 50,000 for certain information-only filings), using the official Form T1 or the Banco de España's electronic platform. Documentary retention for audit purposes is mandatory for six years, evidencing invoice, shipping document and receipt of funds in accordance with the agreed trade terms.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium as a sole treasury spine; Medium-High as an ancillary payment and FX lane. Non-EU digital EMI/banking platforms must hold an electronic-money institution licence in a EEA jurisdiction and either passport into Spain under the EMD2 regime or rely on local branch licensing by Banco de España. Spanish AML Circular 6/2018 and the ISO 20022 creditor-finder requirements require a Spanish IBAN for payroll/direct-debit circuits, so an offshore EMI without an EU passport cannot be the primary clearing rail. Such EMIs can, however, be used for low-value consumer merchant settlement, card acquiring settlement and cross-border supplier payments if connected through a Spanish licensed partner bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is technically permitted under Spanish AML regulations where identity is confirmed via an accredited EU-certified digital-identification signature and biometric video conference. In practice, premier Spanish banks require in-branch physical attendance by at least one director (or, in case of a non-resident sole director, a locally appointed commercial attorney under a powers-of-attorney regime) for the first KYC interview when the UBO is a foreign legal entity. Banco Santander and BBVA have accepted remote on-boarding for non-EU directors only when the UBO has an existing relationship with the bank and provides a notarized and apostilled board resolution. To avoid deferral, the company is advised to appoint a Spanish-domiciled secretary or legal representative, submitting the original notarized deeds and the Spanish tax/company register (Registro Mercantil) certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner(s) with tax residence outside the EEA/Eurozone and a legal entity shareholder in a low-corporate-tax or offshore jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full corporate chart of the owning entity, notarised and apostilled constitution documents, register extracts (equivalent of Companies House), valid passports and proof of address, clean NIE/TIE if applicable, and a detailed source-of-wealth declaration with bank-supported asset documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high volume of cross-border e-commerce remittances from multiple PSPs (Stripe, PayPal) with no prior banking history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business plan, audited financials, contractual merchant agreements with Stripe and PayPal, projected and actual settlement statements, product-market description of pet-care devices under ISIC 4791, and a compliant transaction-monitoring and chargeback-remediation programme.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a restricted Spanish SL with minimum capital of only EUR 1 and a new legal entity lacking operational substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Drafted shareholder agreement, bank capital-escrow receipt or notarial deed of contribution, evidence of physical local presence (lease agreement, utility bill), staff contracts or B2B service contracts, and VAT/Intrastat registration confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from customers/suppliers in high-risk third countries or countries subject to FATF/OFAC/EU sanctions owing to global pet-supply procurement (`Pet food`, veterinary devices, China sourcing).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening software logs, Consolidated EU Sanctions list compliance commitment, corporate anti-money-laundering policy, ad-hoc country risk assessment, and commercial trade documents (invoices, contracts, customs declarations) proving end-use and beneficiary verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce chargebacks and refund complexity creating card-acquirer risk and potential negative account metrics.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Delivery/proof-of-delivery records, importation and customs-entry certificates, PSA/Visa network reports, complaint-resolution procedures, and evidence of maintained reserve account with the acquirer to absorb disputed transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for non-resident capital injections into the Spanish SL uses SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Credit Transfer if the shareholder is within the Single Euro Payments Area). Beneficiary must be identified with the full legal name, address (NIF-XXxxxxxx), IBAN ES + 22 digits, and BIC/SWIFT of the Spanish bank. The remittance information field must contain the narrative `APORTACION DE CAPITAL - INCREMENTO DE FONDO DE COMERCIO / SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION` and, if the account is a `Capital Escrow Account`, the reference `CAPITAL ESCROW ACCOUNT`. For investment amounts ≥ EUR 1,000,000, the Spanish recipient must submit the post-transaction foreign-investment declaration (Form D-1A) electronically to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores within one month of registration; for statistical purposes, Bank of Spain's Form T1 is filed when transaction amounts exceed the EUR 50,000 de minimis threshold. Verification includes source-of-funds statements from the investor's bank, evidence of tax residence, an OECD CRS code, and, if applicable, a transfer-pricing documentation file supporting the issuance of equity rather than shareholder loans.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payment of goods to non-EU/third-country suppliers, the treasury should use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers under short open-account terms, supported by invoice, packing list, airway bill/bill-of-lading and a receiving-bank commercial payment undertaking. For high-value procurement of pet devices, an irrevocable Letter of Credit issued on the Spanish corporate bank's SWIFT network through the advised/confirming bank under UCP 600 is the preferred rail. EU suppliers are paid via SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) using the supplier's IBAN within the SEPA zone. For retail refunds and chargeback settlement in the e-commerce inbound flows, use the card-network reconciliation rails (Visa/Mastercard) and/or PayPal settlement links, with settlement in EUR, while any chargeback must be recorded only after card-acquirer reserve rules have been complied with.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD FX forwards outright under an ISDA 2002 or a Spanish Treasury Mirror Agreement, requiring no upfront premium and covering trade-payables within a 12-month horizon.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies that are not freely deliverable (e.g., CNY, MXN, BRL, RUB if permitted by sanctions) where settlement is in EUR/USD, allowed for hedging commercial exposures with non-residents.
Cross-currency swaps for the exchange of EUR and USD interest flows on any trade or invoice-finance facility, requiring EURIBOR/SOFR benchmark incorporation and central clearing under EMIR rules.

FX swaps/rollovers for short-term treasury conversion to cover import receivables/payables up to 30-90 days, executed on an unsecured ISDA or via the bank's FX e-platform, optimizing pre-trade and post-trade margin under SFTR.

FX options (call/put structures) on EUR/USD, such as plain vanilla options and collars, permissible as documented hedging against foreign-currency cash-flow uncertainty but requiring the Spanish company to evidence an underlying commercial exposure and to execute through a regulated Spanish investment services firm.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 20 July (fixed calendar deadline for calendar-year fiscal period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines ranging from €100 to €5,000+, potential escalation to mercantile registry administrative strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts with Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholders' meeting approval of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €3,000, possible administrative sanctions and company strike-off after prolonged non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if net turnover exceeds €8 million, total assets exceed €4 million, or average number of employees exceeds 50 during the fiscal year (Pyme exemption thresholds)
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Pyme accounting standards (adapted General Accounting Plan for SMEs)

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual confirmation or filing required; beneficial ownership register must be updated immediately upon any change in shareholding, UBO composition or corporate structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General corporate income tax rate is 25%. Newly created SL entities may benefit from a reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable income and 20% on the excess for the first two tax periods with positive taxable income. R&D and technological innovation tax credits are available. No sectoral tax holiday applies to pet supplies electronic retailing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200: Corporate Income Tax return. Filed electronically through the AEAT portal at www.agenciatributaria.gob.es using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or authorized representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For calendar year-end SLs, the ordinary deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss for the tax period before corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must reconcile with the statutory annual accounts of the Spanish SL. No branch accounting is permitted; the SL is a Spanish tax resident and reports its worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Positive and negative tax adjustments to accounting profit, including permanent and temporary differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible payments to foreign related parties, unjustified management fees, and expenses without supporting economic substance. Arm's length evidence must be kept for any cross-border related party invoice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior year tax losses against the current positive taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Spanish SL tax losses are eligible. Losses of foreign shareholders or related foreign companies cannot be transferred into Spain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable income after loss offset and tax base refinements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm statutory offset limits by net turnover: applicable restrictions may limit loss offset for taxpayers with revenue above EUR 20 million or EUR 60 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross corporate tax amount at the applicable rate before credits and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Spanish domestic credits and treaty credits properly documented may reduce the gross tax. Foreign shareholders cannot inject credits earned abroad into the Spanish SL return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax liability, payments on account, prior withholdings, and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review all cross-border dividend, interest, and royalty payments made by the SL. Where a non-resident shareholder claims treaty relief, the corresponding documentation must be in the SL's tax file before settlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers graduated surcharges under Article 27 LGT: 5% of the tax amount within 3 months, 10% within 6 months, 15% within 12 months, and 20% after 12 months, plus daily late-payment interest. Filing after an AEAT assessment request carries a minimum penalty of 50% of the resulting tax amount. Incorrect or omitted data may attract fixed penalties under Articles 199 and 200 LGT.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 24% statutory general non-resident withholding tax on dividends; 19% for residents of EU/EEA states with effective tax information exchange; 0% for qualifying EU parent shareholders holding at least 5% of the Spanish SL for 12 months under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate, the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the Spanish SL payer with: a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) for the payment year; a beneficial ownership declaration; a tax identification number or NIE; and written instruction before withholding. The payer may apply the treaty rate at source only with complete documentation. If excess withholding has occurred, the non-resident files Modelo 210 with AEAT, attaches the TRC, and claims the refund within the applicable limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 19% for EU/EEA beneficial owners and 24% for other non-residents on interest and royalties. Under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive, 0% applies to qualifying associated EU companies with at least 25% direct control and substance. Tax treaties may further reduce rates, typically to 0-15% depending on the residence jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is required where related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 per transaction type and related party. Master File documentation is required where the foreign or consolidated group has net turnover exceeding EUR 45 million. Lower-volume transactions still require contemporaneous arm's length evidence where they affect the Spanish taxable base.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not apply Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the same economic substance principles operate through Article 15 LGT general anti-avoidance rules, OECD principal purpose test, and Spanish case law. The SL must have real commercial activity, local management, operational premises or logistics, employees, customer contracts, and risk-bearing functions. A mailbox company or a shell SL created solely to access Spanish e-commerce or DTA benefits will be challenged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting sales collected through Stripe or PayPal, overstating deductible costs, using false invoices, or hiding the identity of the ultimate non-resident beneficial owner while continuing to operate the Spanish SL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty under LGT Articles 191-193 from 50% to 150% of the tax amount at stake plus late-payment interest. Where the evaded tax exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal tax evasion under Article 305 Criminal Code carries imprisonment from 1 to 5 years and fines up to six times the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal secondary liability for unpaid corporate tax debts under Article 42 LGT when the corporate veil is pierced. In fraud cases, directors risk civil restitution, asset freezes, travel bans, disqualification from managing companies, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Spanish SL without employees, physical premises, stock, logistics, books and records, or local decision-making, while claiming tax treaty benefits and routing e-commerce sales through related entities abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may disregard the SL as fictitious, reattribute business revenues to the real parent entity, disallow deductions, deny DTA benefits, and impose penalties from 50% to 150% of the reassessed tax. Corporate law sanctions for false registered office or artificial single-purpose structures can reach EUR 60,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may lift the corporate veil and impose joint and several liability on directors and shareholders. Serious structuring fraud can lead to criminal charges, travel restrictions, and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform customer due diligence, ignoring unusual online payment patterns, accepting large cash payments above Spanish legal thresholds, or using non-transparent payment intermediaries to avoid traceability of e-commerce revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 10/2010, minor AML infringements attract fines from EUR 600 to EUR 60,000; serious infringements attract fines from EUR 60,001 to EUR 1,500,000 or up to 5% of own funds. SEPBLAC and AEAT may impose additional tax penalties for undeclared payment gateway receipts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally fined, disqualified from corporate management, and criminally prosecuted under Criminal Code Articles 301/302 for money laundering, with imprisonment from 1 to 6 years and substantial fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive intercompany royalties, management fees, marketing commissions, or inflated product costs to a related foreign supplier in order to strip profit out of the Spanish SL without arm's length documentation or economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may recharacterize the transactions under Article 18 LGT, make a downward adjustment to deductible expenses, assess additional corporate income tax at 25%, apply penalty rates of 50-150%, and deny treaty relief. If the stripped profit is material and intentional, criminal tax liability may also arise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute sham agreements or false invoices are jointly and severally liable for the corrected tax debt. They also face insolvency disqualification, travel bans, and personal imprisonment where the profit stripping amounts to tax evasion.
